A profile's name was always yours to choose, and still is. Nothing said what
the names mean, though, so this release writes that down and teaches `pack` the
one name it should not hand over without asking.

### Changed

- A bundle that would carry `@personal` asks before it is written, whether that
  profile came from `--only` or from the file having one at all:

  > ```
  > @personal is yours, not the team's, and a bundle hands it to whoever opens it. [UNDERSTOOD/N]
  > ```

  `personal` is the name for a key each person holds their own copy of, a seat
  on an API they pay for themselves, so a bundle takes one only when someone
  says the word. The question needs a terminal, which is what keeps a script
  from packing another person's keys by itself, and the refusal names the
  profiles the file has besides it:

  > ```
  > monkeys: nothing written. to pack the rest: monkeys pack --only @test,production
  > ```

  A project whose file declares no `@personal` packs exactly as it did.

### Documentation

- [The usual
  names](https://docs.monk3ys.dev/docs/concepts/profile/#the-usual-names):
  `test` holds the keys that can leak without anyone being woken, `production`
  the real ones, `staging` a deployment that is not production, and `personal`
  a key each person holds their own copy of. `monkeys` checks a name against
  none of this; a name a reader already knows is the whole point.

- `test` goes at the top, and goes there even when it arrives after the others,
  since the first profile is the one a command takes when none is given. Names
  go in full: a prefix is enough to type, so `@p` already reaches
  `@production`, and `prod` costs the reader without buying the writer
  anything.
